name: indian stuffed poblanos
instructions:
Two variants: A is the STUFFED-POBLANO build — Priya Krishna's original transcribed in full, with my additions and my full from-scratch execution; B is the QUESADILLA variant.

=== VARIANT A — PRIYA KRISHNA'S WHITE BEAN–STUFFED POBLANOS (TRANSCRIBED) ===

Serves 4.

INGREDIENTS:
- 1/4 cup + 1 tablespoon olive oil, divided
- 2 teaspoons cumin seeds
- 2 small yellow onions, finely diced
- 2 tablespoons ground coriander (freshly ground is best)
- One 15-ounce can great northern beans, drained and rinsed
- 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more if needed
- 1 small indian green chile or serrano chile, finely chopped
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice (from about 1 lime), plus lime wedges for serving
- 1 pound small poblano peppers of roughly the same size (2 to 3 ounces each), slit lengthwise

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.
2. In a large skillet over medium-high heat, warm 1/4 cup of the oil. Once the oil begins to shimmer, add the cumin seeds and cook until they turn a medium shade of brown, about 1 minute max. Add the onions and coriander and cook, stirring, until the onions are translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from the heat and let the mixture cool to room temperature.
3. While the onions cool, mash the white beans with a potato masher or fork in a medium-size bowl until they have the consistency of chunky mashed potatoes. Add the salt, chile, garlic, lime juice, and cooled onions and mix well. Taste and adjust the salt if needed.
4. Divide the filling evenly among the poblanos, using a small tablespoon to stuff the filling into each nook and cranny of the peppers.
5. Arrange the stuffed poblanos slit-side up on a baking sheet. Drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil. Bake for 45 minutes, or until the poblanos have shriveled and wrinkled at the area around the slits and turned dark green. Serve garnished with lime wedges.

MY ADDITIONS TO VARIANT A: I like braising it in cream or milk, adding fennel/clove-like spices, and putting cream cheese in the peppers as well for tang (bland without).

--- MY FULL STUFFED BUILD (VARIANT A WITH THE ADDITIONS, FROM SCRATCH) ---

Roasted poblanos stuffed with a white-bean filling built on from-scratch indian spice work, bound with cream cheese, finished with lime.

--- PREP ---

- Preheat oven to 400°F.
- Prep the poblanos: HALVE lengthwise and seed them, OR stuff whole with the stem/top cut off — use judgement based on the specific poblanos (see notes). Don't parboil.
- Start the poblanos baking while you make the filling.

--- THE FILLING ---

1. BLOOM WHOLE SPICES in vegetable oil over medium heat: whole cardamom, cinnamon stick (broken), whole cloves, fennel seeds. Just briefly, until fragrant.
2. Add minced garlic (non-negotiable — see notes) and cook another minute.
3. Add ground spices: cumin, coriander, turmeric, and GARAM MASALA (non-negotiable). Toast in the oil.
4. No fresh onion at any stage — see notes.
5. Add white beans and cook, mashing them as you go. Add splashes of milk as needed to keep the bottom from burning while you mash and cook the funk out of the beans.
6. Season with salt to taste (no pre-salted paste is doing that work).
7. When the bean paste tastes done (smooth, no raw-bean character), fold in CREAM CHEESE to taste — 1/8 to 1/4 of a block, or two large spoonfuls. Don't be too delicate.
8. Stuff the poblanos, return to the oven, finish until done. Some bean paste will leak out — that's fine.
9. FINISH WITH LIME at the plate (or into the filling at the very end). Cilantro over the top if you have it.

=== VARIANT B — THE QUESADILLA VARIANT ===

Largely the same filling as the stuffed build, reworked for a tortilla. Verdict: it works well, but the spice stack is still uncertain (see notes).

The changes from the stuffed build:
1. THE BASE: finely process a SHALLOT + POBLANO + GARLIC as the base (no vessel here — the poblano moves into the filling itself).
2. CILANTRO goes in, BRAISED IN THE CREAM.
3. THE CHEESE: MONTERREY JACK instead of cream cheese.
4. LEMON/LIME JUICE REQUIRED.
5. NO TURMERIC — keep the clean white/green colors.
6. SPICE STACK (UNCERTAIN): coriander, cloves, lemon zest, and fennel push it indian; without them it could easily drift mexican, which is also fine.

Assemble and cook as a quesadilla in tortillas.
notes:
=== SOURCE — PRIYA KRISHNA, NOW TRANSCRIBED IN FULL AS VARIANT A ===

Priya Krishna's 'White Bean–Stuffed Poblanos' is transcribed in its entirety as variant A (previously only cited, never captured). My additions when making her version: braising it in cream or milk, fennel/clove-like spices, and cream cheese in the peppers for tang (bland without). Those same additions are what grew into my full stuffed build (recorded under variant A):
1. CREAM CHEESE as the binding fat.
2. The FENNEL/CLOVE whole-spice stack (the cardamom/cinnamon/cloves/fennel bloom).
3. Milk/cream in the filling.

From her headnote: her mom invented the dish after forgetting to buy potatoes for the stuffing and subbing white beans mixed with lots of garlic and cumin-coated onions — the white beans get even softer and creamier in the oven and absorb the flavors of the poblanos. Also from the book: the leftover white-bean stuffing makes an excellent dip.

=== THE CORE — CHEESE + LIME + POBLANO + STARCH ===

The structural core of the dish: CREAM CHEESE (the binding fat), LIME (the acid finish, non-negotiable), POBLANO (the vessel — the namesake), and A STARCH (the white beans). Everything else is seasoning architecture on top.

=== LIME IS NON-NEGOTIABLE — THIS DISH IS WHERE LIME SHINES ===

Squeeze fresh lime over the stuffed poblanos at the plate (or into the filling at the very end). The cream cheese + roasted poblano + spiced filling combination all read RICHER, ROUNDER, and MORE INTEGRATED when the lime hits — the acid cuts the dairy and lifts the pepper's smoky-grassy character without competing with anything. One of the recipes in the cookbook where lime is doing structural work rather than just brightening. In the STUFFED BUILD, don't substitute lemon — lemon's rounder acid reads wrong against the poblano; lime's citrus-forward, slightly floral edge is what pairs. The QUESADILLA VARIANT is the exception: lemon/lime juice required, either works there (and lemon zest is part of its indian-pushing spice stack).

CILANTRO IS NICE-TO-HAVE: a scatter of fresh chopped cilantro at serving reads noticeably fresher and more finished. Not required.

=== POBLANO IS THE CENTER OF GRAVITY — DAIRY IS THE BINDER ===

The poblano is the dish's structural and flavor anchor; the filling exists to bridge the pepper's smoky-grassy character with a creamy fat. That binder is CREAM CHEESE — no exceptions. Coconut milk doesn't work here (proven in the removed massaman variant, where it would normally have paired beautifully); the poblano wants dairy, not coconut.

=== HALVE OR STUFF WHOLE — USE JUDGEMENT BASED ON THE POBLANO ===

Poblanos have a weird topology — some are curvy but flat, others rounder:
- HALVE LENGTHWISE: for poblanos rounded or deep enough to hold filling as boats. Presents cleanly.
- STUFF WHOLE: cut off the top/stem, seed through the opening, pack from the top. Better for flat-shaped poblanos. Slightly messier.

NEVER PARBOIL: poblanos get soggy faster than thicker-walled bell peppers; parboiling collapses their structure. Roast them dry from the start.

WHY POBLANO, NOT JALAPEÑO: wall thickness for stuffing, heat low enough to eat as a main, smoky-grassy character that bridges with dairy. Baked jalapeños are too spicy as a main, and baking them releases capsaicin aerosols that irritate eyes and lungs. Not worth the kitchen suffering.

=== SPICE WORK — THE WHOLE-SPICE BLOOM IS THE POINT ===

- BLOOM WHOLE SPICES FIRST: whole cardamom, cinnamon stick, whole cloves, fennel seeds in oil before the ground spices. Skip the bloom and the filling collapses toward generic-indian.
- GROUND SPICE MIX: cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala — added after the bloom, before the beans. GARAM MASALA IS NON-NEGOTIABLE — the ground-spice glue that ties the bloom to the beans.
- GARLIC IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: it builds the aromatic-savory base from scratch.
- NO FRESH ONION (MY STUFFED BUILD ONLY): the white-bean + cream cheese + indian-spice combination reads clean and integrated without it; onion introduces texture and sweetness that fight the smooth mash. Garlic carries the allium slot alone. Two exceptions: Priya's original runs on cumin-coated onions (yellow onions, olive oil, and the green chile/serrano live in secondary for her transcription only), and the quesadilla variant runs on a finely processed shallot in its base.
- SALT TO TASTE: nothing pre-salted in the build — season the filling yourself.

=== BEAN MECHANICS ===

- WHITE BEANS, NOT CHICKPEAS OR LENTILS: white beans mash into a smooth filling-shape; chickpeas stay too discrete, lentils go too loose.
- MILK FOR DEGLAZING THE MASH: small splashes keep the bottom from burning and help cook the funk out of the beans.

=== WANT TO TRY — POTATOES ===

Potatoes as a filling component (parboiled, cubed small so they integrate with the bean mash). Provenance: potatoes were the ORIGINAL plan in Priya's family version — the white beans were the forgot-to-buy-potatoes substitution that stuck. A mexican-shaped sibling recipe — parboiled potatoes + red chile paste (guajillo/ancho) + cream cheese in the same poblano format — is the other direction, but that would be its own recipe, not a variant of this one.

=== VARIANT B — THE QUESADILLA: SPICE STACK UNCERTAIN, COLORS DELIBERATE ===

It works well, but I'm uncertain on the spice stack. CORIANDER, CLOVES, LEMON ZEST, AND FENNEL push it indian; without them it could easily drift mexican, which is also fine — the dish survives either register.

TURMERIC STAYS OUT of the quesadilla on purpose: I like the clean white/green colors (monterrey jack + cream + cilantro + poblano). Turmeric belongs to the stuffed build only.

MONTERREY JACK is the quesadilla's cheese — cream cheese is the stuffed build's binder; they don't swap across variants.

=== REMOVED VARIANTS (SEPTEMBER 2026) ===

This recipe used to be a three-variant 'stuffed poblanos' master; cleaned up to the single indian build:
- SEED VARIANT (former A — toasted pumpkin/sunflower/sesame seeds + cream cheese, american/mexican-leaning): removed — we don't need it.
- MASSAMAN PASTE VARIANT (former C — Priya's own paste shortcut, 'the most indian thing on the thai shelf'): removed — thai doesn't fit the pantry (massaman recipes retired the same week). The coconut-milk-doesn't-work lesson was proven there.
Full text of both survives in git history.
original_chef: Priya Krishna (variant A is her White Bean–Stuffed Poblanos transcribed in full); variant B is my rebuild with cream cheese as the binder, the fennel/clove whole-spice stack, and a milk/cream braise.
